cases.name: api-dispositions
cases.notes: §4 step 5(b): a block the changeset touched gets a disposition — `edited` when its id was live before and its bytes changed, `inserted` otherwise — confidence 1, reason `api`, matcher_v null; a carried block the changeset left byte-identical in place is `same` and (store 14.2) not persisted, so the heading `b_0` has no row under `c_1`. The commit carries origin `api`, the actor and the reason.

cases.name: conflict-on-third-doc-commits-nothing
cases.notes: §4 step 5 + §10 Fixed (2.1): a changeset is one transaction, one commit. The file-CAS of every loaded document runs before any file is written, so c.md's dirty bytes abort the request before a.md or b.md is touched: no api commit row and no revision of the request lands, the files keep their observed bytes; c.md's disk bytes are ingested (observed, c_3; b_5 pooled) and the request errors sync_conflict. The b_ ids the ops minted at parse time (b_6..b_8) are consumed, so the human line is b_9.

cases.name: observe-after-apply-echoes
cases.notes: §4 step 5: the api commit's `file_hash` is the rendered bytes, so the sync path observing the same bytes afterwards is an echo (no commit).

cases.name: empty-insert-still-commits
cases.notes: §2.1/§4: an empty parse inserts nothing (`ids: []`) but the document was loaded, so it is rendered, written and committed as a new revision with identical content.

cases.name: api-edit-one-of-three-leaves-siblings-same
cases.notes: §4 step 5(b) (store 14.2): one `update` of the beta paragraph. The known-id resolver classifies the carried blocks as the matcher would — the heading, alpha and gamma are `same` (raw bytes, parent and sibling index unchanged) and are not persisted; only `b_2` gets a row, `edited / 1 / api`. Through store 14.1 every carried block was stamped `edited`, so a one-paragraph edit moved every sibling's `updated_at`.
